risks_fired.evidence: 'If nothing earned itself, say so and stop' asks Claude to judge whether the session it co-produced earned a compound; RLHF bias toward finding something means the negative branch fires rarely even on thin sessions. Partially offset by the artifact-level evidence gate ('show me which branch you picked, the moment that earned it, and why') per the evidence-backed-Debrief carve-out — the gate constrains HOW Claude reports, not WHETHER it finds something.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional hardening only if cohorts surface inflated rules: 'if the branch is something any developer would already know, or not specific to THIS codebase from THIS session, say so and stop.' Non-blocking on this non-load-bearing module-close prompt either way.

risks_fired.evidence: Carve-out applied — body blockquote right after the fence ('LLM self-charity may creep in. If the saved rule reads generic, ask for one specific to this session.') names the charity risk and gives a pushback move.
risks_fired.fix_hint: No action needed; the existing body blockquote already does the job.

risks_fired.evidence: 'The file gets the rule alone' is deliberately ambiguous per the prompt registry's own maintainer note on ae101-m2-integrate-branch.md ('Deliberate imprecision — do NOT tighten... wants the student to catch that alone could overwrite ./CLAUDE.local.md and nuke M1's rules'). check_pedagogy.md rule 51 (deliberate-antipattern, flagged-by-design) applies, and the check_prompts.md integrate-verb personal-scope carve-out separately applies (body lead-in says 'integrate'; fence carries 'personal file, not team ./CLAUDE.md' + 'create + gitignore if missing'). Body callout right after the fence ('Watch the diff: integrating should add the new rule, not overwrite') further neutralises it.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Leave as-is — tightening the wording removes the precision-prompting lesson this beat exists to teach (per the registry's own maintainer note).

risks_fired.evidence: Same evidence and carve-out stack as file-preservation-gap — personal-scope + create-if-missing narrows the destructive branch; the risk is the intended M2 lesson, not an accident.
risks_fired.fix_hint: No action needed — same rationale as file-preservation-gap.

risks_fired.evidence: Conditional structure ('If one branch... write; if nothing, say so and stop') could invite reasoning-aloud, but the body primer right after the fence ('Feel free to jump direct at the diff in ./CLAUDE.local.md; Claude's preamble is optional reading') satisfies check_prompts.md rule 17(b)'s skim-past-primer carve-out.
risks_fired.fix_hint: No action needed; existing skim-past primer covers it.

risks_fired.evidence: Body callout 'Watch the diff: integrating should add the new rule, not overwrite ./CLAUDE.local.md' asks the student to manually catch a correctness defect (check_pedagogy.md rule 30 territory). check_pedagogy.md rule 51 deliberate-antipattern exemption applies: the diff-watch is the detection mechanism for the same deliberately-ambiguous 'alone' wording documented in the registry's maintainer note, not an independent defect.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Accepted-by-design per rule 51; no fix owed. If cohorts show students skipping the diff-watch, consider a stronger imperative rather than removing the ambiguity.
